title: Peter Focus.
author: Tshiamo Ramokgadi
body:
# Peter, Focus*.*

The sun is out, the birds are singing hallelujah, and there I am, riding away all my problems. It's a Saturday morning and I'm on my way to the gym.

I get there and the first thing that hits me is the numbers. How is it this packed on a Saturday morning? Side note: either people in Cape Town are genuinely obsessed with being healthy, or we do this because we can't afford every other activity. You tell me which one it is.

Anyway, the gym, the gym. I'm planning and preparing my sets for the day, and honestly this is the exciting part. This is where you visualise before you put in the effort. Every piece of equipment looks like an adventure, and your discipline hasn't been tested yet. This is also the part where, even in life, the dreamers get separated from the executors. It's where so many of us get stuck. In my head, that plan had me giving Solomon a run for his wealth. No pun intended.

Now I want to shift your attention for a moment. Picture yourself in a boxing ring. Ahead of you are all the hurdles and opposition you need to get through to reach the other side. Rep by rep, you start slicing away at these giants. Here's what I found profound: sometimes it feels like nothing is happening.

So there I am, taking on one giant at a time, like David telling Saul about the lion and the bear:

*"And David said unto Saul, Thy servant kept his father's sheep, and there came a lion, and a bear, and took a lamb out of the flock: and I went out after him, and smote him, and delivered it out of his mouth: and when he arose against me, I caught him by his beard, and smote him, and slew him."* (1 Samuel 17:34-35 KJV)

That's often how our reps feel in the gym. But I want us to zoom out and see our lives in this picture. There are days you show up and it feels like nothing is happening. Yet the more you show up, the greater your character and your stamina, until one day, like David, you can confidently declare your works before kings.

But that's not the focus here.

## The treadmill

The focus comes at the end. Lying ahead of me was the dreaded treadmill. My goal was to complete my 10K, and I was pumped. This was my last hurdle, my last mountain. I got onto that bad boy and started running, one leg after the other, one step after another. At first it all felt so good. I was finding my mojo and my rhythm.

But there's a pattern I've come to learn about myself, especially on the treadmill: I get bored. And when I get bored, I lose focus.

Every runner will tell you that somewhere along a marathon route, it stops being about ability and starts being about the mind. It becomes about how badly you want it. And sadly, that's the exact point where I crumbled. A few kilometres from my target, I got tired of the consistency. I started looking elsewhere. I started peeping at how fast my neighbour was going. The very thing that had carried me this far, steady and consistent, became my stumbling block.

And in that moment I heard the Holy Spirit say: **"Peter, focus!"**

The minute I lost my mental fortitude, I forgot my goal. I went from striding long and wide to slowing down, and boom, I hit my face on the roller and bounced off like a ball. Dream shattered, minor injury, bruised ego. It's funny until it happens to you.

Are there circumstances that are simply inevitable? I agree there are. But I've learned that even in our walk with Christ, we all have a part to play.

## This is a word for someone in this season

If you pause, you'll realise this metaphor is a reality in our lives. Many of us have been blessed, or have worked our way into prominent positions, and God is asking one thing of us: focus. The good Lord has you reading this because the consistency and focus you've been practising is exactly what you'll need in the next season He's taking you into. In these last months of the year, let's just focus.

## Peter on the water

Remember Peter? Jesus called him out of the boat, and Peter was bold enough to take the first step.

*"And Peter answered him and said, Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water. And he said, Come. And when Peter was come down out of the ship, he walked on the water, to go to Jesus. But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me. And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him, and said unto him, O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?"* (Matthew 14:28-31 KJV)

Look closely. Peter had the faith to step onto the water, but he needed focus to keep walking on it. The wind didn't appear after he sank. It was blowing the whole time. What changed was where his eyes were. He stopped looking at the One who called him and started looking at the storm.

## What does this look like on a Tuesday?

Because let's be honest, most of our storms don't look like waves. They look like this:

**Your boss is on your case.** Every email feels like criticism and every meeting feels like a trial. You're tempted to shrink, to quit in your heart before you quit on paper. But you were placed in that seat for a reason. Keep your eyes on Jesus and do the work with excellence anyway.

**The work is just hard.** You're learning something new, you feel behind, and everyone else seems to be catching on faster. That's your neighbour's treadmill, not yours. Stay in your lane and keep your pace.

**Nothing seems to be happening.** You've been praying, saving, studying, serving, and the breakthrough still hasn't shown up. Maybe the excitement of the start has worn off and all that's left is the long, quiet middle. That's where most people lose it. Remember the reps: nothing visible doesn't mean nothing is growing.

**Someone else got the thing you asked God for.** A promotion, a relationship, a house, a baby. The comparison creeps in, and suddenly you're peeping at the next treadmill instead of finishing your own race.

*"Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith."* (Hebrews 12:2 KJV)

He started this with you, and He will finish it. Your job is to keep looking at Him.

## One last thing

I fell. Peter started sinking. But you don't have to, and even if you do, He's already reaching.

Whatever the wind is doing right now, whether it's your boss, your bank account, your inbox, or your own doubts, you are so close to your greatest miracle. Plant your eyes firmly on Jesus, and on Him alone.

I don't know who you are, but I need you to focus.

I love you, and I thank God for your life.

Selah. Mo
